title: BYD Files Composite Sulfide Solid-State Electrolyte Patent — Targets 2027 Pilot Production
detail: BYD published patent CN121983643A with China's National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) on May 25, 2026, covering a composite solid electrolyte membrane that combines inorganic solid electrolyte particles (sulfide-based) with a polymer electrolyte fibre network. The architecture addresses two of the key failure modes in pure sulfide solid electrolytes: brittleness under mechanical stress and sensitivity to atmospheric moisture, both of which drive up manufacturing cost through the need for ultra-dry room production environments. BYD's composite approach embeds the sulfide particles within a flexible polymer matrix, improving mechanical compliance while retaining the high ionic conductivity (>10⁻³ S/cm at room temperature) characteristic of sulfide electrolytes. BYD's chief scientist had previously confirmed the company's solid-state development is at a 'critical breakthrough stage,' and the patent filing is consistent with a 2027 pilot production target for sulfide-based all-solid-state cells. The filing places BYD in direct competition with Toyota, Samsung SDI, and QuantumScape for the sulfide solid-state design space — the variant most widely considered closest to commercialization due to its high conductivity. BYD's massive manufacturing base and vertically integrated supply chain (it mines, processes, and manufactures its own battery materials) would give it significant cost advantages in scaling a sulfide solid-state cell if the composite electrolyte engineering challenges can be solved. The patent was filed alongside a broader surge in global solid-state battery IP activity: Q1 2026 saw over 1,710 solid-state battery patent applications published globally, with China accounting for approximately 35% of the portfolio — though analysts warn that patent volume does not guarantee commercialization success.

title: China Leads Global Solid-State Battery Patent Count but Analysts Warn of Losing Technological Edge
detail: A research analysis published May 25, 2026 reviewed the global solid-state battery patent landscape and found China holding approximately 35% of over 1,710 solid-state battery patent applications published in Q1 2026 alone — a dominant position by volume. However, the analysis warned that raw patent count does not reflect technological depth: China's solid-state patents are concentrated in electrode materials and cell architecture, while Japan (Toyota, Idemitsu), South Korea (Samsung SDI, LG Energy Solution), and the United States (QuantumScape, Solid Power, Argonne National Lab) hold proportionally higher shares of foundational electrolyte chemistry and manufacturing process IP. The report flagged specific risks: Chinese companies have achieved high energy density in small-format cells but have not demonstrated large-format automotive cell durability at commercial production yields; the US and Europe are accelerating with substantial government funding (DOE Battery500 Consortium, EU Horizon Europe battery programme); and Japanese manufacturers hold the most mature solid-state pilot production lines (Toyota, TDK). Separately, DigiTimes reported on May 25 that the US is accelerating a strategic shift toward fourth-generation lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry specifically to circumvent Chinese battery patents — a 'G2 Lithium' framework aimed at building a domestically competitive LFP supply chain independent of Chinese IP. The dual dynamic — China dominating patent volume while competitors focus on manufacturing execution and IP circumvention — defines the strategic battlefield for the global battery industry in 2026.
